extraction_note: TDG 10-K is deliberately diversified — no named Pentagon Program Elements, no specific named DoD programs, no specific PE numbers. The company explicitly emphasizes that ~100 manufacturing facilities supply ~100,000 aircraft with no single customer >10% of net sales. The J-Book divergence pattern (named PE → unfunded) materially DOES NOT APPLY structurally to TDG, but the cohort discipline requires us to extract and test what J-Book-grounded claims exist. We extract: (1) defense market revenue concentration claim (43%), (2) generic DoD program participation claims tied to 'multiple platforms', and (3) installed-base / aftermarket forward narrative as it pertains to the defense aerospace market. Control: aftermarket forward narrative, top-10 customer concentration, and DART acquisition.

claims.claim_text: Defense market (defense OEMs + aftermarket sales to U.S. and friendly foreign governments) accounted for approximately 43% of net sales for fiscal year 2022.
claims.subject: TransDigm Group
claims.object_value: 43% of FY2022 net sales from defense market
claims.source_quote: the defense market (which includes defense OEMs and aftermarket sales to the U.S. and friendly foreign governments), which accounted for approximately 43% of our net sales for fiscal year 2022

queries.rationale: Test whether any J-Book PE attributes TransDigm as a primary contractor — would corroborate or undercut the 43% defense-market claim with a forward-funding view.
Confirm scale of DoD contract obligations to TransDigm subsidiaries — does the 43% claim square with public DoD contract awards?

claims.claim_text: We expect defense market net sales to account for a percentage of total net sales relatively in line with our historical levels (29-37%) prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, with fiscal 2022 defense sales of 43% trending down from 50% in fiscal 2021.
claims.subject: TransDigm Group
claims.object_value: defense ~29-37% historically; trending back down post-COVID
claims.source_quote: As the commercial aerospace industry continues to recover, we expect defense market net sales to account for a percentage of total net sales that is relatively in line with our historical levels prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. We began to see this expected trend in fiscal 2022, as defense sales represented 43% of net sales compared to 50% of net sales in fiscal 2021. ... In fiscal years 2015 through 2019, defense market net sales ranged from 29% to 37% of total net sales.
claims.predicate_resolved: forward defense % of total net sales

queries.rationale: Check whether any TransDigm-attributed Pentagon PEs are growing/steady (which would corroborate the 'trending toward historical levels' narrative) or whether the J-Book corpus shows TransDigm-named programs being cut.

claims.claim_text: We provide components to a large and growing installed base of aircraft, supplying aftermarket products to an estimated over 100,000 commercial transport, regional transport, military and general aviation fixed wing turbine aircraft and rotary wing aircraft.
claims.subject: TransDigm Group
claims.object_value: >100,000 aircraft installed base across multiple platforms (military included)
claims.source_quote: We estimate that our products are installed on over 100,000 commercial transport, regional transport, military and general aviation fixed wing turbine aircraft and rotary wing aircraft.

queries.rationale: Diversified-installed-base claim implies exposure across many platforms; check J-Book for any TransDigm-named PEs and assess concentration risk.

claims.claim_text: Recent DOD budgets have trended upwards, but military spending outlook remains uncertain due to government funding reprioritization (e.g., shifting funds to combat COVID-19 and to assist Ukraine in the Russia/Ukraine conflict).
claims.subject: TransDigm Group
claims.object_value: DOD budgets trending upward but reprioritization risk noted
claims.source_quote: For a variety of reasons, the military spending outlook is very uncertain, though recent DOD budgets have trended upwards. ... delays in government spending outlays and government funding reprioritization, such as shifting funds to efforts to combat the impact of the pandemic or efforts to assist Ukraine in the Russia and Ukraine conflict, provides for further unpredictability in the military spending outlook.

queries.rationale: Top-level DOD budget posture — check whether J-Book corpus shows any aerospace component PEs tied to TransDigm that contradict the 'budgets trending up' narrative.

claims.claim_text: Our top ten customers for fiscal year 2022 accounted for approximately 41% of our net sales; no single customer individually accounted for greater than 10% of net sales.
claims.subject: TransDigm Group
claims.object_value: Top-10 = 41% of FY22 net sales; no >10% customer
claims.source_quote: Our top ten customers for fiscal year 2022 accounted for approximately 41% of our net sales. ... None of our customers individually accounted for greater than 10% of our net sales for fiscal year 2022.

queries.rationale: Public DoD contract awards orthogonally cross-check the customer-concentration claim; DoD itself is one customer channel via multiple buying agencies.

claims.claim_text: Approximately 90% of net sales for fiscal year 2022 were generated by proprietary products, and approximately 55% from aftermarket — historically more stable than OEM sales.

queries.rationale: Aftermarket revenue on military platforms is structurally insulated from new-program-of-record funding fluctuations; J-Book check still warranted for any TransDigm-attributed PEs.
